quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Stay closest to the traffic control device.
Stay at the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. The biggest danger is oncoming cars turning left in front of you.

questions.question: What is true about improper braking on a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually has no serious consequences.
It is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle. Which lane position is safest?
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Good riders change position based on traffic and road conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually safest.

questions.question: What type of footwear should a motorcycle rider wear?

options.text: Shoes that are below the ankles.
Boots or shoes that cover the ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover the ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, what happens?

options.text: They are less dangerous than using either one alone.
Their effects cancel each other out.
Their effects become stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects become stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, make riding unsafe. Combining drugs with alcohol makes the danger even worse.

questions.question: Compared to a car, how often does a motorcycle need maintenance?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent maintenance than cars. It is critical to spot problems before riding in traffic or at highway speeds.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you are in a separate lane.
Yes, because it blocks the wind.
No, because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. A driver might not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane without knowing you are there.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Where should a motorcycle passenger sit?
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the rider and hold firmly to the rider's waist, hips, or midsection. They can hold handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, what should you do with the gears?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What should you be aware of while riding?

options.text: Only what is in front of you.
What is both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Look ahead on the road, but also check your mirrors often to see what is behind you.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other beverages?

options.text: It needs to be digested first.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It is absorbed directly into the bloodstream through the stomach and small intestine, and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: What type of gloves should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They improve your grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing to be more visible. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, what gear should the engine be in?
questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
To look for dark clouds that may mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see vehicles coming up behind you. This helps you know if drivers see you and are paying attention to your actions.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before entering any turn or curve.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it then re-apply it. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Grabbing the front brake or slamming the rear brake can:

options.text: Be the best way to stop in an emergency.
Be the best way to slow down when streets are wet.

questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or slamming the rear brake can lock the brakes. This causes control problems.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or always unsafe. Change your position in the lane based on the conditions around you.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies.
Should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: The right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar strong material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, and green. These colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means stop. It works the same as a red traffic light. Wait for a green arrow before turning.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors can adequately show you your surroundings.
Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
Activate your turn signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even when using your mirrors.

questions.question: When is there less traction for braking?

options.text: A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Not change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. Speeding up will not help—they will just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What should you do on a slippery surface?

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to be out of the way of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake is ineffective on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What can long-term exposure to wind noise do?

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise exposure can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when riding. It will protect your hearing while still letting you hear sirens and horns.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that it works before every ride.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to ride right after it starts raining?

options.text: Some other drivers may not react quickly enough to the rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.explanation: The pavement is very slippery right after rain starts. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, mixing with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.
